review: Live controls expose Observe/Suggest through the runtime account feature policy, clamp other requested authorities to Observe, withhold unresolved-policy visual capture, expose explicit local playback mute, and add a Shared Live Rooms opt-in switch. Program-action and room consent grants remain separate.

Local playback mute changes the local audio element only. Provider output remains available to the separately admitted Discord bridge. Audio-focus loss still mutes playback; focus restoration respects the local mute setting. The hook reapplies mute to a replacement controller on explicit renewal while microphone and visual sharing start disabled.

Runtime fix 34 binds Rooms status reads and opt-in results to account identity/revision, request generation and mounted state. Account change clears the old view, mutation supersedes older status reads, and focus does not compete with a pending mutation. Four prior failing cases are covered by its retained baseline.

Runtime fix 35 retires pending session start on Stop/unmount, cleans up a late admitted exact session, rejects duplicate pending starts, and isolates attempt-owned controller/handler cleanup. Provider callbacks ignore retired attempts. Route/account changes cancel an in-flight request as well as an active call.

Transport startup has its own generation guard around microphone acquisition, offer/description awaits and SDP exchange. Stop retires pending work; late microphone tracks are stopped before WebRTC is created. Late events and failures cannot affect a successor transport. Three previously failing runtime cases were observed across the hook and controller baselines.

Reviewed candidate deltas and surrounding policy, renewal, start/stop, provider callbacks and media-resource handlers. New Rooms component/suites, local-playback and cancellation suites were read. Three unchanged transport suites and unchanged audio-focus/account helpers retain exact public/indexed parity. No provider credentials, real transcripts, profiles, media recordings or third-party implementation are exported.

The older visual-consent test double lacked the new setLocalPlaybackMuted method and failed all four existing tests. Its fixture now implements that method; restored visual-consent checks and new renewal/cancellation checks run against the real hook. That fixture failure is not counted as a runtime defect.
limits: Unfrozen unpublished source-only proposal. Runtime fixes 34 and 35 are not installed; a matching numbered build/domain and signed ordinary-account acceptance remain required.

Tests use mocked provider/server/native/media boundaries. Playback checks establish local routing and focus behavior, not actual Discord sound. No real microphone, model run, room change, Minecraft action or attended GPT Live handoff occurred.
Late server-session cleanup is best effort and remains exact-session/account authorized. Ignoring a retired opt-in response cannot undo a server mutation already accepted before the account changed.
The Rooms status payload retains its existing typed transport contract; malformed payloads, every account/session interleaving and all provider/network failure modes are not qualified by this suite.

Full app, real provider consent, expiry/revocation timing, browser permission prompts and installed native handling remain separate acceptance. Source compilation does not replace those checks or certify program effects.

The Live provider-event/worker implementation and larger Console integration remain later source cohorts. Canonical shared contracts, domain and native dependencies are not copied automatically. Five intentional support-contact matches elsewhere remain in final publication review.
